subject: Literature
title: Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
description: A 60-second lesson on Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.

hook.text: Louisa May Alcott did not want to write Little Women. Her publisher insisted, and she wrote it under protest.

buildup.text: The novel follows the four March sisters growing up during the Civil War, navigating ambition, love, and independence.

discovery.text: Jo March, the tomboyish writer, became literature's first aspirational female character for millions of young women.

twist.text: Alcott hated the conventional marriage ending but wrote it because her publisher demanded Jo marry someone.

climax.text: Little Women showed that stories about girls' inner lives could be universal literature, not niche entertainment.

punchline.text: She wrote it under protest, and it became immortal.

quiz.question: Why did Alcott write the marriage ending reluctantly?
options: She wanted Jo to marry a different character
Her publisher demanded Jo marry someone despite Alcott's objections
She believed the story needed a tragic ending instead
